## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

 Within the Pali tradition, its verses resemble *Dhammapada* verse 94 (Dhp 94). Further resembling verses are found across northern and Indic transmission lineages, notably in the Patna Dharmapada (P-Dhp 84–95, *Śokavagga*), the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 19 / UVS 19, *Aśvavarga*), the Tibetan translation (Uv Kg 19), and several Chinese translations including the *Faju jing* (T 210.15, T 210.31), the *Chu yao jing* (T 212.20), and the *Fa ji yao song jing* (T 213.19).

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
